patch.author: Christopher Owen <christopherowen@users.noreply.github.com>, Sun, 8 Nov 2026 18:50:51 +0000 (kept)
patch.applies_on: candidate-49 0762..0766 (git am, tree equal to the tested one) and bare 1107 (git apply --check)

root_cause: The first revision validated its _local_mask cache entries with mask._version (cache[key] = (mask, mask._version, local), router.py:203). The vLLM worker runs every forward under torch.inference_mode, the startup profile_run included; the routed mask _routing_masks computes there (torch.empty_like in _masks) is an inference tensor, which tracks no version counter, so reading _version raised RuntimeError on the first SP route_local of the profile run, on every rank (sp5 TP0, sp6 TP1, sp7 TP2, both starts). The PR's tests and bench ran outside inference mode. A second defect in the same change: with no ForwardContext the cache and the image mask fell back to sp_rows, a frozen dataclass, so assigning raised FrozenInstanceError (not reached in serving, which always has a context; reached by any caller outside a forward).
change: Cache entries live only on the forward's ForwardContext (the passed context or the current one) and are keyed by (id(mask), num_tokens, world_size, rank, rows, pad); the entry holds the mask, and a hit requires entry[0] is mask. No version counter is read. Outside a forward nothing is cached, and _routing_masks keeps the image mask on the context only, as 1107 does. The pad=True polarity fix in _partials_mask and the slicing are unchanged.
why_not_stale: Lifetime: the runner creates a new ForwardContext for every forward (set_forward_context -> create_forward_context), so no entry outlives its forward; the runner's persistent is_padding and input_ids buffers keep their storage across steps but each forward starts with an empty cache.
Identity: the entry holds the mask tensor, so its id cannot be reused by another tensor while the entry lives; entry[0] is mask is checked.

Contents: within a forward, is_padding and input_ids are filled before the forward runs (input preparation, DeadRows included) and not written during it. 1107 already relies on this: it keeps routed = ~is_padding and the image mask on ForwardContext keyed by tensor identity alone. routed and image are new tensors each forward (torch.empty_like) that nothing writes after their kernel.
Layout: num_tokens, world_size, rank, rows and pad are in the key, so another layout in the same forward (CED compact rows, a drafter) gets its own entry.

Tested: test_gate_router_route_local_masks_last_one_forward refills persistent padding and id buffers in place across three forwards under inference mode and checks each forward routes with its own masks.

parts.detail: TP3 tail rank per-call: T=1024 1.30x, 2048 1.13x, 4096 1.07x, 16384 1.016x faster beyond the recorded 1107 interval; T=8192 1.02x within it (boot1 231.8 us vs 1107 231.0/230.6, boot2 220.9), the cell where the original gained only 1.015x. No tail cell is worse, and none is slower than the original #996 on per-call timing. Under inference mode, in process, 5 of 5 tail cells are faster beyond the interval on both boots (1.02x..1.21x per call).

reason: The boot failure is the cache's mask._version read on inference tensors. Keying the cache on the forward's own ForwardContext and the mask's identity, with no version read, is valid under torch.inference_mode and cannot serve another forward's masks; it keeps the PR's bit-exactness and its TP3 tail-rank route_local gain (4 of 5 cells beyond the recorded interval, T=8192 within and not worse; 5 of 5 under inference mode in process). The fallback to caching on the frozen SPRows is removed.
caveats: T=8192 (TP3 tail) is within the recorded interval on the no_grad bench; this is reported, not re-run.

Non-tail ranks: per-call 6 faster, 11 within, 6 slower than the recorded 1107 boots (slower by 0.3-4 us, <= 1.9%), the cache lookup where local_slice is already a view; the original's own mark showed the same pattern (4 slower). Under inference mode in process: 22 within, 1 slower. Skipping the cache when the slice is a view would remove this; not done, to keep the rework to the defect.

The harness uses a stand-in ForwardContext and plain scratch, as the PR's tests do; it does not run the SP gather collective or a real engine boot. A cluster boot of the corrected stack (tp3-switched) remains to be done in a candidate window.
